cards.text: Friend, the WHOLE nation of Israel has just finished crossing the Jordan River. Now the LORD speaks to Joshua, Israel's leader. Choose twelve men, He says, one from each tribe.

cards.question: The LORD has a job for those twelve men. What are they supposed to take up from the middle of the Jordan?
The twelve men are supposed to take them from the very spot where the priests were standing in the Jordan. True or false?

cards.text: So Joshua sends the twelve men back into the middle of the Jordan, each to take a stone up on his SHOULDER. Friend, that's not a pebble you slip in your apron pocket.

cards.question: Joshua says the stones will serve as a sign among Israel. Who does he say will one day ask what the stones mean?
When someone asks about the stones, Joshua tells Israel to answer that they won a great battle. True or false?
The waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the LORD, so Joshua says the stones will be a ___ to the Israelites forever.

cards.text: And the Israelites do exactly as Joshua commanded, just as the LORD had told him. Twelve stones come up out of the middle of the Jordan, one for each tribe of Israel.

cards.question: Where do the Israelites carry the twelve stones from the river and set them down?

cards.text: But Joshua isn't done with stones yet. He also sets up twelve stones himself.

cards.question: Where does Joshua set up these twelve stones?

answers.text: In the middle of the Jordan where the priests stood
On the riverbank facing the city of Jericho
On top of a hill looking over the camp

cards.text: And the writer says those stones are there to this day. So where have the priests with the ark been all this time?

cards.question: While the people finish everything the LORD commanded Joshua to tell them, where are the priests carrying the ark?

answers.text: Standing in the middle of the Jordan

cards.text: It's all done just as Moses had directed Joshua, and the people hurried across. Nobody's stopping in that riverbed for a selfie, friend.

cards.question: Once everyone has finished crossing the Jordan, what do the priests with the ark of the LORD do?

answers.text: They cross over while the people watch
They stay in the river overnight
They go back to the east side

cards.text: Now meet the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, the tribes whose land is back on the east side of the Jordan. They cross over ahead of the rest of Israel, as Moses had instructed them.

cards.question: The Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh cross ahead of the other Israelites. How do they go?

cards.text: About 40,000 troops armed for battle cross over before the LORD into the plains of Jericho. Friend, I get nervous when TWO bakers walk in at once.
On that day, the LORD does something for Joshua in the sight of all Israel.

cards.question: On the day Israel crosses the Jordan, what does the LORD do for Joshua in the sight of all Israel?

answers.text: He gives him a new name

cards.question: Israel revered Joshua all the days of his life, just as they had revered ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Joshua to command the priests who carry the ark of the Testimony to come up from the Jordan.
So Joshua commands the priests, "Come up from the Jordan." Up they climb with the ark, and their feet touch the dry land.

cards.question: The moment the priests carrying the ark step onto dry land, what happens to the Jordan?

answers.text: The waters return and overflow the banks
The riverbed stays dry until morning
The waters stand up in a heap again

cards.text: On the tenth day of the first month, the people go up from the Jordan and set up camp on the eastern border of Jericho.

cards.question: On the tenth day of the first month, where does Israel camp, on the eastern border of Jericho?
At their new camp, Joshua sets up the twelve stones they took from the Jordan. True or false?

cards.text: Then Joshua says that one day their children will ask their fathers, 'What is the meaning of these stones?' Chip used to beg me for one more story every night, and these stones are built to start one.

cards.question: Joshua tells the fathers what to answer: Israel crossed the Jordan on ___ ground.
Joshua says the LORD dried up the Jordan just as He once dried up another body of water. Which one?
Joshua tells Israel why the LORD dried up the Jordan. What reason does he give?

answers.text: So all peoples know His hand is mighty
So Israel could rest before the battle
So the priests could reach Jericho first

cards.text: Now the Amorite kings west of the Jordan and the Canaanite kings along the coast hear how the LORD dried up the Jordan before the Israelites. I bet that news moved faster than a group chat.

cards.question: When the Amorite and Canaanite kings hear how the LORD dried up the Jordan, how do they react?

answers.text: They gather their armies to attack
They send gifts asking for peace

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. Israel's across, the stones are standing, and trust me, friend, this story's not done.

findings.problem: This is a where question, but both wrong answers are made-up places ('On the riverbank facing the city of Jericho', 'On top of a hill looking over the camp'). Neither is a real location detail from the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The joke 'Nobody's stopping in that riverbed for a selfie' puts a modern phone inside the Bible scene. It blends the comparison with the Bible setting instead of keeping a separate everyday image.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The card says these are 'the tribes whose land is back on the east side of the Jordan.' That fact comes from outside the passage (Num 32; Josh 1:12-15) and has no reference. The card cites only Joshua 4:12.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke compares 40,000 armed troops crossing to battle with two bakers walking into his bakery and making him nervous. Those aren't the same action, so it doesn't click right away. It also has him nervous about bakers arriving, which clashes with his warm welcome for every baker.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The Chip line ('these stones are built to start one') is sweet but not funny. It reads like a nice dad being pleasant on one of the walkthrough's few personality beats.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Joshua 4:24 gives two reasons the LORD dried up the Jordan. The second, 'so that you may always fear the LORD your God', is never told on any card, and this card asks for only one reason.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The card cites Joshua 5:1 but tells nothing from 5:1. Its content ('Israel's across, the stones are standing') comes from earlier verses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Along with the story-isn't-over line, the card adds a recap ('Israel's across, the stones are standing') instead of moving the passage along.
